decisions.reason: The Ocisen fleet is verified, but civilian production and distribution are not.
decisions.analysis: Fleet strength and alien alliances do not establish a post-work arrangement or a human-person proxy.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper lore reading under the pace instruction.

decisions.reason: The publisher verifies corporate extraction, without a demonstrated post-work or deliberate job-preservation mechanism.
decisions.analysis: Predatory ownership and advanced spacecraft alone do not qualify the colonies; the synopsis concerns soldiers and colonial output.
decisions.follow_up: Keep as a corporate-extraction comparison; skip novel reading.

decisions.reason: Edenist wealth, living habitats and consensus politics do not yet establish employment-independent basic access.
decisions.analysis: The helium-3 monopoly and real democratic consultation are distinct from an automated household-support entitlement. Affinity-linked human personalities are not automatically an external AI government.
decisions.follow_up: Skip the trilogy investigation; reopen only on a concise source explaining production and resident access.

decisions.reason: Adamist worlds are a heterogeneous political aggregate, without one evidenced post-work economy.
decisions.analysis: Mechanical technology and membership in the Confederation do not transfer Edenist institutions or a uniform guarantee to all Adamist worlds.
decisions.follow_up: Skip this broad aggregate rather than inventing a common coordinate.

decisions.reason: Tranquillity is an identifiable living habitat, but its general allocation rules remain unverified.
decisions.analysis: Its non-Edenist status prevents borrowing Edenist consensus politics. A prosperous research habitat does not itself establish wage-independent provision for all residents.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper reading; do not infer guarantees from habitat life support.

decisions.reason: The Kiint claim to be beyond economics, but the short reference does not resolve their actual later institutions.
decisions.analysis: The initially presented species account is not enough to identify the final population, support mechanism or distribution of control; a justified alien-person proxy would also be required.
decisions.follow_up: Skip a late-novel reconstruction; reopen only on clear setting documentation.

decisions.reason: Utopial distinctness is verified; the quick post-scarcity label does not establish the actual distribution mechanism.
decisions.analysis: Building habitats and describing a project as post-scarcity leave broad resident access, automation and effective productive control unresolved.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper reading; do not borrow Corporate Earth or later exodus institutions.

decisions.reason: Olyix medical trade and captive transport do not document a supported free resident post-work population.
decisions.analysis: A technological pilgrimage and captured people cannot be converted into universal security or a nonworking census; the human setting label is not the Olyix economy.
decisions.follow_up: Keep as a coercive-technology comparison and move on.

decisions.reason: Human exodus is verified, but this broad lead lacks a particular settled allocation system.
decisions.analysis: Flight, long-term survival and later military strength do not establish whether a named enclave distributes essentials independently of work.
decisions.follow_up: Skip reconstruction across the trilogy and its changing timelines.

decisions.reason: Prime biological specialization does not establish autonomous production for a separately supported leisure population.
decisions.analysis: Immotiles and motiles may be parts of a collective organism rather than independent rulers and automated servants. Counting stationary minds as nonworkers would prejudge the person denominator.
decisions.follow_up: Preserve as a distributed-organism comparison; skip deeper reading.

review_notes: Fast reference-led dispositions; no novel read, decoding, PDF rendering or access-denial workaround.
No new record is forced from advanced transport, wealth, a military fleet, a post-scarcity label or a biological division of labor.
The user explicitly accepts skipping obscure lore rather than spending substantial time rescuing a candidate.
